::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 6th 1892  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Girton College Cambridge, Yonge IV 28
:::

Dear [Mr Innes](people/person_744.qmd),
Votes coming straight to me, and votes going first to [Miss Coleridge](people/person_329.qmd) made a certain amount of confusion - and four for [Rowling Manor](other_books/otherbook_647.qmd) dated Jany 30th, came in just at the end and carried it up to 14 votes while [L’Epine Noble](other_books/otherbook_662.qmd) has twelve --- So I suppose it must be the prize one, though my own judgment would not have gone that way.[^1]

Thank you about the stamps   -   We will divide

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: This relates to the prize for the best story in the Christmas 1891 number of the [*MP*](organizations/other_52.qmd).  Readers were asked to vote for their favourite.
